title: The Beacon That Walked Out — How the US sided with Russia and North Korea at the UN
narrative: The US delegation walked out of a UN Security Council meeting on Monday, in protest at comments by France that compared Washington's human rights voting to authoritarian states. The row started when the US joined North Korea and Russia in voting against extending Volker Turk's term as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. France's UN mission posted: 'The US used to be a beacon of human rights. Not anymore.' US ambassador Mike Waltz accused France of voting for a human rights chief who had been 'lecturing' democratic countries while 'cozying up to the world's worst oppressors.' US ambassador Dan Negrea said the delegation will continue similar protests until France 'renounces their condescending and disrespectful rhetoric.' US ambassador Jeff Bartos warned 'there will be consequences' and threatened to reassess US UN engagement and funding. The vote was 144 in favour, 10 against, 13 abstentions.
telemetry: US voted alongside North Korea and Russia against UN High Commissioner for Human Rights — states that rank among the world's worst human rights violators
Vote tally: 144 states in favour, only 10 against (US, Russia, North Korea, Iran, Syria, Belarus, Eritrea, Nicaragua, Venezuela, Myanmar), 13 abstentions
France's UN mission direct response: 'The US used to be a beacon of human rights. Not anymore.' — a stinging rebuke from a NATO ally
US not only voted against the commissioner but walked out of Security Council to avoid hearing France's remarks — a diplomatic tantrum by a permanent member
US ambassador explicitly threatened to cut UN funding: NYT reports Trump admin cut 40% of voluntary UN contributions in FY2026
Context: US simultaneously waging war in Iran, walking out of human rights mechanisms, and lecturing Iran on human rights violations
Universal Periodic Review: US up for review in 2025 — verify how many recommendations the Trump admin accepted vs. rejected
analysis:
The vote tally tells the story before any commentary. 144 states voted to extend Volker Turk's term. Ten voted against: the United States, Russia, North Korea, Iran, Syria, Belarus, Eritrea, Nicaragua, Venezuela, and Myanmar. That is the company the United States chose to keep at the UN this week.

France's response — 'The US used to be a beacon of human rights. Not anymore.' — came from a NATO ally, not an adversary. That distinction matters. When an ally publicly states what was previously whispered in diplomatic corridors, the mask has slipped. The US delegation's response was not to engage the criticism but to walk out of the Security Council chamber to avoid hearing it. A permanent member of the Security Council, with veto power over international peace and security, fled the room rather than listen to a fellow democracy speak the truth.

The threat to cut funding — the US has already cut 40% of voluntary UN contributions — uses financial coercion rather than diplomatic persuasion. This is not leadership. This is the behavior of a state that has lost the moral argument and resorts to its wallet.

The timing compounds the contradictions. The US is simultaneously prosecuting a war against Iran — a regime it criticizes for human rights violations — while voting alongside that same regime against the UN's top human rights official. The lecture on Iranian human rights abuses and the vote against the international mechanism that documents human rights abuses cannot both be serious positions.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: The US joined Russia, North Korea, Iran, Syria, Belarus, Eritrea, Nicaragua, Venezuela, and Myanmar in voting against the UN's top human rights official. 144 states voted the other way. When France — a NATO ally — said 'The US used to be a beacon of human rights. Not anymore,' the US delegation walked out of the Security Council rather than hear the truth. The company you keep says more than the speeches you give.
